text: In relation to a building, includes an addition or extension to a building.

heading: Aluminium Composite Panel (ACP)
text: Flat or profiled aluminium sheet material in composite with any type of materials.

heading: Amenity
text: An attribute which contributes to the health, physical independence, comfort and well-being of people.

heading: Ancillary components
text: A component of the building that is not required to ensure the stability of the building or structure as a whole (that is, not part of the primary structure), but which must still withstand all actions.

heading: Ancillary element
text: An element that is secondary to and not an integral part of another element to which it is attached.

heading: Annual exceedance probability
text: The probability that a given rainfall total accumulated over a given duration will be exceeded in any one year.

heading: Annual greenhouse gas emissions
text: The theoretical amount of greenhouse gas emissions attributable to the energy used annually by a building's services, excluding kitchen exhaust and the like.

heading: Appropriate authority
text: For the purposes of the Fire Safety Verification Method, means the relevant authority with the statutory responsibility to determine the particular matter satisfies the relevant Performance Requirement.

heading: Appropriate authority
text: The relevant authority with the statutory responsibility to determine the particular matter.

heading: Appropriately qualified person
text: A person recognised by the appropriate authority as having qualifications and/or experience in the relevant discipline in question.

heading: Approved disposal system
text: A system for the disposal of sewage, sullage or stormwater approved by an authority having jurisdiction.

heading: Articulated masonry
text: Masonry construction in which special provisions have been made for movement by articulation.

heading: Assembly building
text: A building where people may assemble for—

heading: Assessment Method
text: A method that can be used for determining that a Performance Solution or Deemed-to-Satisfy Solution complies with the Performance Requirements.

heading: Assumed cooling thermostat set point
text: The cooling thermostat set point used to calculate cooling degree hours, and equal to 17.8+0.31Tm, where Tm is the mean January outdoor air temperature measured in degrees Celsius.

heading: Atrium
text: A space within a building that connects 2 or more storeys and—

heading: Atrium well
text: A space in an atrium bounded by the perimeter of the openings in the floors or by the perimeter of the floors and the external walls.

heading: Automatic
text: Designed to operate when activated by a heat, smoke or fire sensing device.

heading: Available safe egress time (ASET)
text:
(1) The time between ignition of a fire and the onset of untenable conditions in a specific part of a building.
(2) The time referred to in (1) is the calculated interval between the time of ignition of a fire and the time at which conditions become such that the occupant is unable to take effective action to escape to a place of safety.

heading: Average daylight factor
text: The ratio of the illumination level within a room provided by daylight to the level of daylight outside the building during overcast conditions.

heading: Average specific extinction area
text: The average specific extinction area for smoke as determined by AS 5637.1.

heading: Backflow prevention device
text: An air gap, break tank or mechanical device that is designed to prevent the unplanned reversal of flow of water or contaminants into the water service or a Network Utility Operator’s water supply.

heading: Backpressure
text: A reversal of water flow caused by the downstream pressure becoming greater than the supply pressure.

heading: Backsiphonage
text: A reversal of flow of water caused by negative pressure in the distributing pipes of a water service or supply.

heading: Backstage
text: A space associated with, and adjacent to, a stage in a Class 9b building for scenery, props, equipment, dressing rooms, or the like.

heading: Battery system
text: One or more chemical cells connected in series, parallel or a combination of the two for the purpose of electrical energy storage.

heading: Blockage
text: An obstruction within a water service or sanitary plumbing or drainage system.

heading: Boiler
text: A vessel or an arrangement of vessels and interconnecting parts, wherein steam or other vapour is generated, or water or other liquid is heated at a pressure above that of the atmosphere, by the application of fire, the products of combustion, electrical power, or similar high temperature means, and—

heading: Bond breaker
text: A material used as part of a waterproofing system that prevents the membrane bonding to the substrate, bedding or lining.

heading: Breaking surf
text: Any area of salt water in which waves break on an average of at least 4 days per week but does not include white caps or choppy water.

heading: Building complexity criteria
text: Are used to determine the building complexity level of all or part of a building in accordance with Table 2, where building complexity criteria are as follows:

heading: Buried rainwater tank
text: A rainwater tank that is set into and completely covered by earth.

heading: Burnout
text: Exposure to fire for a time that includes fire growth, full development, and decay in the absence of intervention or automatic suppression, beyond which the fire is no longer a threat to building elements intended to perform load bearing or fire separation functions, or both.

heading: Carpark
text: A building that is used for the parking of motor vehicles but is neither a private garage nor used for the servicing of vehicles, other than washing, cleaning or polishing.

heading: Cavity
text: A void between 2 leaves of masonry, or a void between the cladding and the supporting frame, the primary insulation layer or the outermost control layer.

heading: Cavity wall
text: For the purposes of F1V1 and H2V1, a wall that incorporates a drained cavity.

heading: Certificate of Accreditation
text: A certificate issued by a State or Territory accreditation authority stating that the properties and performance of a building material or method of construction or design fulfil specific requirements of the NCC.

heading: Certificate of Conformity
text: A certificate issued under the ABCB scheme for products and systems certification stating that the properties and performance of a building material or method of construction or design fulfil specific requirements of the NCC.

heading: Certification body
text: A person or organisation operating in the field of material, product, form of construction or design certification that has been accredited by the Joint Accreditation System of Australia and New Zealand (JAS-ANZ), and is accredited for a purpose other than as part of the CodeMark Australia Certification Scheme or WaterMark Certification Scheme.

heading: Characteristic
text: The occupant data to be used in the modelling of access solutions which define how an occupant interacts with a building, i.e. occupant movement speeds, turning ability, reach capability, perception of luminance contrast and hearing threshold.

heading: Clad frame
text: Timber or metal frame construction with exterior timber or sheet wall cladding that is not sensitive to minor movement and includes substructure masonry walls up to 1.5 m high.

heading: Climate specific part load value
text: A metric for the efficiency of a connected group of chillers that accounts for the Energy Efficiency Ratio of the chillers operating to meet the design load and specified part-load ratios.

heading: Climate zone
text: An area defined in Figure 2 and in Table 3 for specific locations, having energy efficiency provisions based on a range of similar climatic characteristics.

heading: Collected
text: For the purposes of Section F in NCC Volume One, the interception of water —

heading: Combustible
text: Applied to—

heading: Common wall
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Condensation
text: The formation of liquid water on the surface of a building element or material as a result of moist air coming into contact with a surface which is at a lower temperature.

heading: Conditioned space
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Construction activity actions
text: Actions due to stacking of building materials or the use of equipment, including cranes and trucks, during construction or actions which may be induced by floor to floor propping.

heading: Containment protection
text: The installation of a backflow prevention device at the point of connection of a Network Utility Operator’s water supply to a site.

heading: Contaminant
text: Any substance (including gases, liquids, solids or micro-organisms), energy (excluding noise) or heat, that either by itself or in combination with the same, similar or other substances, energy or heat, changes or is likely to change the physical, chemical or biological condition of water.

heading: Control layer
text: Any continuous layer that is installed for one or more of the purposes of air, water, vapour or thermal control, including pliable building membrane and sarking-type material but excluding waterproofing membranes or the like complying with AS/NZS 4858.

external_refs.title: Wet area membranes

heading: Controlled fill
text: Material that has been placed and compacted in layers with compaction equipment (such as a vibrating plate) within a defined moisture range to a defined density requirement.

heading: Cooling degree hours
text: For any one hour when the mean outdoor air temperature is above the assumed cooling thermostat set point, the degree Celsius air temperature difference between the mean outdoor air temperature and the assumed cooling thermostat set point.

heading: Cooling load
text: The calculated amount of energy removed from the cooled spaces of the building annually by artificial means to maintain the desired temperatures in those spaces.

heading: Critical radiant flux (CRF)
text: The critical heat flux at extinguishment (CHF in kW/m2) as determined by an Accredited Testing Laboratory in accordance with AS ISO 9239.1.

heading: Cross-connection
text: Any actual or potential connection between a water supply and any contaminant.

heading: Curtain wall
text: A non-load bearing external wall that is not a panel wall.

heading: Daily outdoor temperature range
text: The difference between the maximum and minimum temperatures that occur in a day.

heading: Damp-proof course (DPC)
text: A continuous layer of impervious material placed in a masonry wall or pier, or between a wall or pier and a floor, to prevent the upward or downward migration of water.

heading: Deemed-to-Satisfy Provisions
text: Provisions which are deemed to satisfy the Performance Requirements.

heading: Deemed-to-Satisfy Solution
text: A method of satisfying the Deemed-to-Satisfy Provisions.

heading: Defined flood event (DFE)
text: The flood event selected for the management of flood hazard for the location of specific development as determined by the appropriate authority.

heading: Defined flood level (DFL)
text: The flood level associated with a defined flood event relative to a specified datum (see Figure 3).

heading: Dehumidification gram hours
text: For any one hour when the mean humidity is more than 15.7g/kg, the grams per kilogram of absolute humidity difference between the mean outdoor absolute humidity and 15.7g/kg.

heading: Designated bushfire prone area
text: Land which has been designated under a power of legislation as being subject, or likely to be subject, to bushfires.

heading: Design bushfire
text: The characteristics of a bushfire, its initiation, spread and development, which arises from weather conditions, topography and fuel (vegetation) in a given setting, used to determine fire actions.

heading: Design fire
text: The quantitative description of a representation of a fire within the design scenario.

heading: Design scenario
text: The specific scenario of which the sequence of events is quantified and a fire safety engineering analysis is conducted against.

heading: Design wind speed
text: The design gust wind speed for the area where the building is located, calculated in accordance with AS/NZS 1170.2 or AS 4055 (see Table 4 for wind classes).

external_refs.title: Wind loads for housing (incorporating amendment 1)

heading: Detention centre
text: A building in which persons are securely detained by means of the built structure including a prison, remand centre, juvenile detention centre, holding cells or psychiatric detention centre.

heading: Direct fix cladding wall
text: For the purposes of F1V1 and H2V1, means a wall with cladding attached directly to the wall framing without the use of a drained cavity.

heading: Discontinuous construction
text: Means—

heading: Display glazing
text: Glazing used to display retail goods in a shop or showroom directly adjacent to a walkway or footpath, but not including that used in a café or restaurant.

heading: Domestic services
text: The basic engineering systems that use energy or control the use of energy; and—

heading: Drainage
text: Any part of—

heading: Drainage flange
text: A flange connected to a waste pipe, at the point at which it passes through the floor substrate, to prevent leakage and which enables tile bed drainage into the waste pipe.

heading: Drainage riser
text: A waste pipe between the floor waste and the drainage system.

heading: Drainage system
text: A system that—

heading: Drained
text: For the purposes of Section F in NCC Volume One, the removal to a drainage system, water that has been collected and redirected.

heading: Drinking water
text: Water intended primarily for human consumption but which has other domestic uses.

heading: Early childhood centre
text: Any premises or part thereof providing or intending to provide a centre-based education and care service within the meaning of the Education and Care Services National Law Act 2010 (Vic), the Education and Care Services National Regulations and centre-based services that are licensed or approved under State and Territory children's services law, but excludes education and care primarily provided to school aged children in outside school hours settings.

heading: Effective height
text: The vertical distance between the floor of the lowest storey included in the calculation of rise in storeys and the floor of the topmost storey (excluding the topmost storey if it contains only heating, ventilating, lift or other equipment, water tanks or similar service units).

heading: Efficacy
text: The degree to which a system achieves a design objective given that it performs to a level consistent with the system specification during the relevant fire scenario.

heading: Electricity network substation
text: A building in which high voltage supply is converted or transformed and which is controlled by a licensed network service provider designated under a power of legislation.

heading: Electric passenger lift
text: A power-operated lift for raising or lowering people in a car in which the motion of the car is obtained from an electric motor mechanically coupled to the hoisting mechanism.

heading: Electrohydraulic passenger lift
text: A power-operated lift for raising or lowering people in a car in which the motion of the car is obtained from the action of liquid under pressure acting on a piston or ram, the pressure being generated by a pump driven by an individual electric motor.

heading: Energy value
text: The net cost to society including, but not limited to, costs to the building user, the environment and energy networks.

heading: Engaged pier
text: A pier bonded to a masonry wall by course bonding of masonry units or by masonry ties.

heading: Envelope
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Equivalent
text: Equivalent to the level of health, safety and amenity provided by the Deemed-to-Satisfy Provisions.

heading: Evacuation route
text: The continuous path of travel (including exits, public corridors and the like) from any part of a building, including within a sole-occupancy unit in a Class 2 or 3 building or Class 4 part, to a safe place.

heading: Evacuation time
text: The time calculated from when the emergency starts for the occupants of the building to evacuate to a safe place.

heading: Exit
text: Means—

heading: Expert judgement
text: The judgement of an expert who has the qualifications and experience to determine whether a Performance Solution or Deemed-to-Satisfy Solution complies with the Performance Requirements.

heading: External wall
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Extra-low voltage
text: A voltage not exceeding 50 V AC or 120 V ripple-free DC.

heading: Fabric
text: The basic building structural elements and components of a building including the roof, ceilings, walls, glazing and floors.

heading: Farm building
text: A Class 7 or 8 building located on land primarily used for farming —

heading: Farming
text: Includes—

heading: Farm shed
text: A single storey Class 7 or 8 building located on land primarily used for farming —

heading: Farm vehicle
text: A vehicle used in connection with farming.

heading: Finished ground level
text: The ground level adjacent to footing systems at the completion of construction and landscaping.

heading: Fire actions
text: Each of the following:

heading: Fire brigade
text: A statutory authority constituted under an Act of Parliament having as one of its functions, the protection of life and property from fire and other emergencies.

heading: Fire brigade station
text: For the purposes of E1D2(1)(b) and I3D9, means a state or territory government operated premises which is a station for a fire brigade.

heading: Fire compartment
text: Either—

heading: Fire growth
text: The stage of fire development during which the heat release rate and the temperature of the fire are generally increasing.

heading: Fire hazard
text: The danger in terms of potential harm and degree of exposure arising from the start and spread of fire and the smoke and gases that are thereby generated.

heading: Fire hazard properties
text: The following properties of a material or assembly that indicate how they behave under specific fire test conditions:

heading: Fire intensity
text: The rate of release of calorific energy in watts, determined either theoretically or empirically, as applicable.

heading: Fire-isolated passageway
text: A corridor, hallway or the like, of fire-resisting construction, which provides egress to or from a fire-isolated stairway or fire-isolated ramp or to a road or open space.

heading: Fire-isolated ramp
text: A ramp within a fire-resisting enclosure which provides egress from a storey.

heading: Fire-isolated stairway
text: A stairway within a fire-resisting shaft and includes the floor and roof or top enclosing structure.

heading: Fire load
text: The sum of the net calorific values of the combustible contents which can reasonably be expected to burn within a fire compartment, including furnishings, built-in and removable materials, and building elements.

heading: Fire-protected timber
text: Fire-resisting timber building elements that comply with Specification 10.

heading: Fire-protective covering
text: Any one or more of the following:

heading: Fire-protected steel
text: Loadbearing wall construction comprising hot rolled or cold formed steel members protected with a fire-protective covering that consists of—

heading: Fire-resistance level (FRL)
text: The grading periods in minutes determined in accordance with Specifications 1 and 2, for the following criteria—

heading: Fire-resisting construction
text: For the purposes of Volume One, means one of the Types of construction referred to in Part C2 of Volume One.

heading: Fire-resisting
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Fire safety engineering
text: Application of engineering principles, rules and expert judgement based on a scientific appreciation of the fire phenomenon, often using specific design scenario, of the effects of fire and of the reaction and behaviour of people in order to—

heading: Fire safety system
text: One or any combination of the methods used in a building to—

heading: Fire-source feature
text: Any one or more of the following:

heading: Fire wall
text: A wall with an appropriate resistance to the spread of fire that divides a storey or building into fire compartments.

heading: Fixed wired
text: For the purposes of Specification 23, a system of electrical wiring (either AC or DC), in which cables are fixed or supported in position.

heading: Flammability Index
text: The index number as determined by an Accredited Testing Laboratory in accordance with AS 1530.2.

heading: Flashing
text: A strip or sleeve of impervious material dressed, fitted or built-in to provide a barrier to water movement, or to divert the travel of water, or to cover a joint where water would otherwise penetrate to the interior of a building, and includes the following:

heading: Flashover
text: In relation to fire hazard properties, means a heat release rate of 1 MW.

heading: Flight
text: That part of a stair that has a continuous series of risers, including risers of winders, not interrupted by a landing or floor.

heading: Flood hazard area
text: The site (whether or not mapped) encompassing land lower than the flood hazard level which has been determined by the appropriate authority.

heading: Flood hazard level (FHL)
text: The flood level used to determine the height of floors in a building and represents the defined flood level plus the freeboard (see Figure 3).

heading: Floor area
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Floor waste
text: A grated inlet within a graded floor intended to drain the floor surface.

heading: Foundation
text: The ground which supports the building (see Figure 5).

heading: Fractional effective dose (FED)
text: The fraction of the dose (of thermal effects) that would render a person of average susceptibility incapable of escape.

heading: Freeboard
text: The height above the defined flood level as determined by the appropriate authority, used to compensate for effects such as wave action and localised hydraulic behaviour.

heading: Fully developed fire
text: The state of total involvement of the majority of available combustible materials in a fire.

heading: Glazing
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Going
text: The horizontal dimension from the front to the back of a tread less any overhang from the next tread or landing above (see Figure 11.2.2f in the ABCB Housing Provisions).

heading: Green Star
text: The building sustainability rating scheme managed by the Green Building Council of Australia.

heading: Group number
text: The number of one of 4 groups of materials used in the regulation of fire hazard properties and applied to materials used as a finish, surface, lining, or attachment to a wall or ceiling.

heading: Habitable room
text: A room used for normal domestic activities, and—

heading: Hazard Rating
text: A level of potential toxicity that may cause contamination in a drinking water system, having a rating of Low Hazard, Medium Hazard or High Hazard, determined in accordance with NCC Volume Three.

heading: Health-care building
text: A building whose occupants or patients undergoing medical treatment generally need physical assistance to evacuate the building during an emergency and includes—

heading: Heated water
text: Water that has been intentionally heated; normally referred to as hot water or warm water.

heading: Heating degree hours
text: For any one hour when the mean outdoor air temperature is less than 15°C, the degrees Celsius temperature difference between the mean outdoor air temperature and 15°C.

heading: Heating load
text: The calculated amount of energy delivered to the heated spaces of the building annually by artificial means to maintain the desired temperatures in those spaces.

heading: Heat release
text: The thermal energy produced by combustion (measured in kJ).

heading: Heat release rate (HRR)
text: The rate of thermal energy production generated by combustion, measured in kW (preferred) or MW.

heading: High Hazard
text: Any condition, device or practice which, in connection with a water supply, has the potential to cause death.

heading: High wind area
text: A region that is subject to design wind speed more than N3 or C1 (see Table 4).

heading: Hob
text: The upstand at the perimeter of a shower area.

heading: Horizontal exit
text: A required doorway between 2 parts of a building separated from each other by a fire wall.

heading: Hours of operation
text: The number of hours when the occupancy of the building is at least 20% of the peak occupancy.

heading: House energy rating software
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Illuminance
text: The luminous flux falling onto a unit area of surface.

heading: Illumination power density
text: The total of the power that will be consumed by the lights in a space, including any lamps, ballasts, current regulators and control devices other than those that are plugged into socket outlets for intermittent use such as floor standing lamps, desk lamps or work station lamps, divided by the area of the space, and expressed in W/m2.

heading: Inclined lift
text: A power-operated device for raising or lowering people within a carriage that has one or more rigid guides on an inclined plane.

heading: Individual protection
text: The installation of a backflow prevention device at the point where a water service connects to a single fixture or appliance.

heading: Insulation
text: In relation to an FRL, the ability to maintain a temperature on the surface not exposed to the furnace below the limits specified in AS 1530.4.

heading: Integrity
text: In relation to an FRL, the ability to resist the passage of flames and hot gases specified in AS 1530.4.

heading: Internal wall
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Interstitial condensation
text: The condensation of moisture on surfaces between material layers inside the building component.

heading: Irrigation system
text: An irrigation system of the following types:

heading: JASANZ
text: The Joint Accreditation System of Australia and New Zealand.

heading: Kerb ramp
text: A ramp incorporated in a kerb.

heading: Lamp power density
text: The total of the maximum power rating of the lamps in a space, other than those that are plugged into socket outlets for intermittent use such as floor standing lamps, desk lamps or work station lamps, divided by the area of the space, and expressed in W/m2.

heading: Landing
text: An area at the top or bottom of a flight or between two flights.

heading: Latent heat gain
text: The heat gained by the vapourising of liquid without change of temperature.

heading: Lateral support
text: A support (including a footing, buttress, cross wall, beam, floor or braced roof structure) that effectively restrains a wall or pier at right angles to the face of the wall or pier.

heading: Lead free
text: Where a plumbing product or material in contact with drinking water has a weighted average lead content of not more than 0.25%.

heading: Lightweight construction
text: Construction which incorporates or comprises—

heading: Loadbearing
text: Intended to resist vertical forces additional to those due to its own weight.

heading: Loadbearing wall
text: For the purposes of H1D4 and H2D3 of NCC Volume Two and Section 4 of the ABCB Housing Provisions, means any wall imposing on the footing a load greater than 10 kN/m.

external_refs.raw_text: and Section 4 of the ABCB Housing Provisions

heading: Loss
text: Physical damage, financial loss or loss of amenity.

heading: Low Hazard
text: Any condition, device or practice which, in connection with a water supply, would constitute a nuisance by colour, odour or taste but does not have the potential to injure or endanger health.

heading: Low rainfall intensity area
text: An area with a 5 minute rainfall intensity for an annual exceedance probability of 5% of not more than 125 mm/hour.

heading: Low-rise, low-speed constant pressure lift
text: A power-operated low-rise, low-speed device for raising or lowering people with limited mobility on a carriage that is controlled by the application of constant pressure to a control.

heading: Low-rise platform lift
text: A power-operated device for raising or lowering people with limited mobility on a platform, that is controlled automatically or by the application of constant pressure to a control.

heading: Low voltage
text: A voltage exceeding extra-low voltage, but not exceeding 1000 V AC or 1500 V DC.

heading: Luminance contrast
text: The light reflected from one surface or component, compared to the light reflected from another surface or component.

heading: Main water heater
text: The domestic hot water unit in a dwelling that is connected to at least one shower and the largest number of hot water outlets.

heading: Main space conditioning
text: Either—

heading: Massive timber
text: An element not less than 75 mm thick as measured in each direction formed from solid and laminated timber.

heading: Maximum retained water level
text: The point where surface water will start to overflow out of the shower area.

heading: Medium Hazard
text: Any condition, device or practice which, in connection with a water supply, has the potential to injure or endanger health.

heading: Membrane
text: A barrier impervious to moisture.

heading: Mezzanine
text: An intermediate floor within a room, that is not separated from that room by walls.

heading: Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS)
text: The Minimum Energy Performance Standards for equipment and appliances established through the Greenhouse and Energy Minimum Standards Act 2012.

heading: Mixed construction
text: A building consisting of more than one form of construction, particularly in double-storey buildings.

heading: Mould
text: A fungal growth that can be produced from conditions such as dampness, darkness, or poor ventilation.

heading: NABERS Energy
text: The National Australian Built Environment Rating Systems for energy efficiency, which is managed by the New South Wales Government.

heading: Network Utility Operator
text: A person who—

heading: Non-combustible
text: Applied to—

heading: Non-drinking water
text: Water which is not intended primarily for human consumption.

heading: Occupant traits
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Occupiable outdoor area
text: A space on a roof, balcony or similar part of a building—

heading: On-site wastewater management system
text: A system that receives and/or treats wastewater generated and discharges the resulting effluent to an approved disposal system or re-use system.

heading: Open-deck carpark
text: A carpark in which all parts of the parking storeys are cross-ventilated by permanent unobstructed openings in not fewer than 2 opposite or approximately opposite sides, and—

heading: Open space
text: A space on the allotment, or a roof or similar part of a building adequately protected from fire, open to the sky and connected directly with a public road.

heading: Open spectator stand
text: A tiered stand substantially open at the front.

heading: Other property
text: All or any of the following—

heading: Outdoor air
text: Air outside the building.

heading: Outdoor air economy cycle
text: A mode of operation of an air-conditioning system that, when the outdoor air thermodynamic properties are favourable, increases the quantity of outdoor air used to condition the space.

heading: Outfall
text: That part of the disposal system receiving surface water from the drainage system and may include a natural water course, kerb and channel, or soakage system.

heading: Overflow device
text: A device that provides relief to a water service, sanitary plumbing and drainage system, rainwater service or stormwater system to avoid the likelihood of uncontrolled discharge.

heading: Panel wall
text: A non-load bearing external wall, in frame or similar construction, that is wholly supported at each storey.

heading: Partially buried rainwater tank
text: A rainwater tank that is not completely covered by earth but is partially set into the ground.

heading: Patient care area
text: A part of a health-care building normally used for the treatment, care, accommodation, recreation, dining and holding of patients including a ward area and treatment area.

heading: Performance-based design brief (PBDB)
text: The report that defines the scope of work for the performance-based analysis, the technical basis for analysis, and the criteria for acceptance of any relevant Performance Solution as agreed by stakeholders.

heading: Performance Requirement
text: A requirement which states the level of performance which a Performance Solution or Deemed-to-Satisfy Solution must meet.

heading: Performance Solution
text: A method of complying with the Performance Requirements other than by a Deemed-to-Satisfy Solution.

heading: Perimeter of building
text: For the purposes of Section 8 of the Housing Provisions, means the external envelope of a building.

external_refs.raw_text: of Section 8 of the Housing Provisions

heading: Personal care services
text: Any of the following:

heading: Piping
text: For the purposes of Section J in Volume One or Part H6 in Volume Two, and Section 13 of the Housing Provisions, means an assembly of pipes, with or without valves or other fittings, connected together for the conveyance of liquids and gases.

external_refs.raw_text: and Section 13 of the Housing Provisions

heading: Pliable building membrane
text: A water barrier as classified by AS 4200.1.

heading: Plumbing
text: Any water service plumbing or sanitary plumbing system.

heading: Plumbing or Drainage Solution
text: A solution which complies with the Performance Requirement and is a—

heading: Point of connection
text: Any of the following:

heading: Predicted Mean Vote (PMV)
text: The Predicted Mean Vote of the thermal perception of building occupants determined in accordance with ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 55.

heading: Preformed shower base
text: A preformed, prefinished vessel installed as the finished floor of a shower compartment, and which is provided with a connection point to a sanitary drainage system.

heading: Pressure vessel
text: A vessel subject to internal or external pressure, including interconnected parts and components, valves, gauges and other fittings up to the first point of connection to connecting piping, and—

heading: Primary building element
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Primary insulation layer
text: The most interior insulation layer of a wall or roof construction.

heading: Private bushfire shelter
text: A structure associated with, but not attached to, or part of a Class 1a dwelling that may, as a last resort, provide shelter for occupants from immediate life threatening effects of a bushfire.

heading: Private garage
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Product
text: Plumbing and drainage items within the scope of Volume Three including but not limited to—

heading: Product Technical Statement
text: A form of documentary evidence stating that the properties and performance of a building material, product or form of construction fulfil specific requirements of the NCC, and describes—

heading: Professional engineer
text: A person who is—

heading: Public corridor
text: An enclosed corridor, hallway or the like which—

heading: Rainwater
text: Naturally occurring water generated by a rain or storm event.

heading: Rainwater service
text: A water service which distributes water from the isolation valve of the rainwater storage to the rainwater points of discharge for purposes such as for clothes washing, urinal and water closet flushing and external hose cocks.

heading: Rainwater storage
text: Any storage of rainwater collected from a roof catchment area which is used to supply water for the primary purposes of drinking, personal hygiene or other uses.

heading: Rapid roller door
text: A door that opens and closes at a speed of not less than 0.5 m/s.

heading: Recognised expert
text: A person with qualifications and experience in the area of plumbing or drainage in question recognised by the authority having jurisdiction.

heading: Redirected
text: For the purposes of Section F in NCC Volume One, the changing of direction of collected water to a drainage system.

heading: Reference building
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Reflective insulation
text: A building membrane with a reflective surface such as a reflective foil laminate, reflective barrier, foil batt or the like capable of reducing radiant heat flow.

heading: Regulated energy
text: The energy consumed by a building's services minus the amount of renewable energy generated and used on site.

heading: Reinforced masonry
text: Masonry reinforced with steel reinforcement that is placed in a bed joint or grouted into a core to strengthen the masonry.

heading: Reliability
text: The probability that a system performs to a level consistent with the system specification.

heading: Renewable energy
text: Energy that is derived from sources that are regenerated, replenished, or for all practical purposes cannot be depleted and the energy sources include, but are not limited to, solar, wind, hydroelectric, wave action and geothermal.

heading: Required
text: Required to satisfy a Performance Requirement or a Deemed-to-Satisfy Provision of the NCC as appropriate.

heading: Required safe egress time (RSET)
text: The time required for safe evacuation of occupants to a place of safety prior to the onset of untenable conditions.

heading: Residential aged care building
text: A Class 3 or 9a building whose residents, due to their incapacity associated with the ageing process, are provided with physical assistance in conducting their daily activities and to evacuate the building during an emergency.

heading: Residential care building
text: A Class 3, 9a or 9c building which is a place of residence where 10% or more of persons who reside there need physical assistance in conducting their daily activities and to evacuate the building during an emergency (including any aged care building or residential aged care building) but does not include a hospital.

heading: Resident use area
text: Part of a Class 9c building normally used by residents, and—

heading: Resistance to the incipient spread of fire
text: In relation to a ceiling membrane, means the ability of the membrane to insulate the space between the ceiling and roof, or ceiling and floor above, so as to limit the temperature rise of materials in this space to a level which will not permit the rapid and general spread of fire throughout the space.

heading: Rise in storeys
text: The greatest number of storeys calculated in accordance with C2D3 of Volume One.

heading: Riser
text: The height between consecutive treads and between each landing and continuous tread.

heading: Rising damp
text: Water absorbed from the ground into a building element.

heading: Rolled fill
text: Material placed in layers and compacted by repeated rolling by an excavator.

heading: Roof light
text: For the purposes of Section J and Part F6 in NCC Volume One, Part H6 in NCC Volume Two, and Part 10.5 and Section 13 of the ABCB Housing Provisions, a skylight, window or the like installed in a roof—

external_refs.raw_text: and Section 13 of the ABCB Housing Provisions

heading: R-Value
text: The thermal resistance of a component calculated by dividing its thickness by its thermal conductivity, expressed in m2.K/W.

heading: Safe place
text: Either—

heading: Sanitary compartment
text: A room or space containing a closet pan or urinal (see Figures 6a and 6b).

heading: Sarking-type material
text: A material such as a reflective insulation or other flexible membrane of a type normally used for a purpose such as waterproofing, vapour management or thermal reflectance.

heading: School
text: Includes a primary or secondary school, college, university or similar educational establishment.

heading: Screed
text: A layer of material (usually cement based) which sets in situ between a structural base and the finished floor material.

heading: Self-closing
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Self-draining
text: A surface finish allowing water to be conveyed by gravity from the finished surface level to the membrane on the top surface of the structural substrate.

heading: Sensible heat gain
text: The heat gained which causes a change in temperature.

heading: Separating element
text: A barrier that exhibits fire integrity, structural adequacy, insulation, or a combination of these for a period of time under specified conditions (often in accordance with AS 1530.4).

heading: Separating wall
text: A wall that is common to adjoining Class 1 buildings (see Figure 7).

heading: Service
text: For the purposes of Section J in Volume One, means a mechanical or electrical system that uses energy to provide air-conditioning, mechanical ventilation, heated water supply, artificial lighting, vertical transport and the like within a building, but which does not include—

heading: Service station
text: A garage which is not a private garage and is for the servicing of vehicles, other than only washing, cleaning or polishing.

heading: Shaft
text: The walls and other parts of a building bounding—

heading: Shower area
text: The area affected by water from a shower, including a shower over a bath and for a shower area that is—

heading: Shower screen
text: The panels, doors or windows enclosing or partially enclosing a shower area.

heading: Single leaf masonry
text: Outer walls constructed with a single thickness of masonry unit.

heading: Site
text: The part of the allotment of land on which a building stands or is to be erected.

heading: Sitework
text: Work on or around a site, including earthworks, preparatory to or associated with the construction, alteration, demolition or removal of a building.

heading: Small-scale Technology Certificate
text: A certificate issued under the Commonwealth Government's Small-scale Renewable Energy Scheme.

heading: Smoke-and-heat vent
text: A vent, located in or near the roof for smoke and hot gases to escape if there is a fire in the building.

heading: Smoke-Developed Index
text: The index number for smoke as determined by an Accredited Testing Laboratory in accordance with AS/NZS 1530.3.

heading: Smoke development rate
text: The development rate for smoke as determined by an Accredited Testing Laboratory testing flooring materials in accordance with AS ISO 9239.1.

heading: Smoke growth rate index (SMOGRA)
text: The index number for smoke used in the regulation of fire hazard properties and applied to materials used as a finish, surface, lining or attachment to a wall or ceiling.

heading: Solar admittance
text: The fraction of incident irradiance on a wall-glazing construction that adds heat to a building's space.

heading: Solar Reflectance Index
text: The solar reflectance index calculated in accordance with ASTM E1980-11(2019).

heading: Sole-occupancy unit
text: A room or other part of a building for occupation by one or joint owner, lessee, tenant, or other occupier to the exclusion of any other owner, lessee, tenant, or other occupier and includes—

heading: Spandrel panel
text: For the purposes of Section J, means the opaque part of a façade in curtain wall construction which is commonly adjacent to, and integrated with, glazing.

heading: Spiral stairway
text: A stairway with a circular plan, winding around a central post with steps that radiate from a common centre or several radii (see Figures 11.2.2d and 11.2.2e in the ABCB Housing Provisions).

heading: Spread-of-Flame Index
text: The index number for spread of flame as determined by an Accredited Testing Laboratory in accordance with AS/NZS 1530.3.

heading: Sprinkler alarm switch
text: For the purposes of Specification 23, a device capable of sending an electrical signal to activate an alarm when a residential sprinkler head is activated (e.g. a flow switch).

heading: Stack bonded pier
text: A pier where the overlap of a masonry unit is not more than 25% of the length of the masonry unit below.

heading: Stage
text: A floor or platform in a Class 9b building on which performances are presented before an audience.

heading: Stairway platform lift
text: A power-operated device for raising or lowering people with limited mobility on a platform (with or without a chair) in the direction of a stairway.

heading: Standard Fire Test
text: The Fire-resistance Tests of Elements of Building Construction as described in AS 1530.4.

heading: Step ramp
text: A ramp, other than a kerb ramp, not exceeding 190 mm in height.

heading: Stormwater
text: Water accumulated or discharged as a result of a rain event.

heading: Storey
text: A space within a building which is situated between one floor level and the floor level next above, or if there is no floor above, the ceiling or roof above, but not—

heading: Structural adequacy
text: In relation to an FRL, means the ability to maintain stability and adequate load bearing capacity as determined by AS 1530.4.

heading: Structural member
text: A component or part of an assembly which provides vertical or lateral support to a building or structure.

heading: Structural substrate
text: The surface of a structural member to be waterproofed as required by Part F1 or F2D2(2)(a).

heading: Sub-surface water
text: Includes—

heading: Surface finish
text: For the purposes of Section F of Volume One, is a material or flooring system directly fixed to or supported above a structural substrate.

heading: Surface water
text: All naturally occurring water, other than sub-surface water, which results from rainfall on or around the site or water flowing onto the site, including water that results from rainfall on the external fabric of the building and any other water that falls or flows onto the fabric from other sources.

heading: Surface water seepage
text: Water escaping through the surface of the ground or a building element.

heading: Swimming pool
text: Any excavation or structure containing water and principally used, or that is designed, manufactured or adapted to be principally used for swimming, wading, paddling, or the like, including a bathing or wading pool, or spa.

heading: Tapered tread
text: A stair tread with a walking area that grows smaller towards one end.

heading: Thermal comfort level
text: The level of thermal comfort in a building expressed as a PMV sensation scale.

heading: Thermal energy load
text: The sum of the heating load and the cooling load.

heading: Threshold ramp
text: A ramp located within or at a threshold.

heading: Total R-Value
text: The sum of the R-Values of the individual component layers in a composite element including any building material, insulating material, airspace, thermal bridging and associated surface resistances, expressed in m2.K/W.

heading: Total Solar Reflectance
text: The complement of the solar absorptance.

heading: Total System Solar Heat Gain Coefficient (SHGC)
text: For the purposes of—

heading: Total System U-Value
text: The thermal transmittance of the composite element allowing for the effect of any airspaces, thermal bridging and associated surface resistances, expressed in Wm-2K-1.

heading: Treatment area
text: An area within a patient care area such as an operating theatre and rooms used for recovery, minor procedures, resuscitation, intensive care and coronary care from which a patient may not be readily moved.

heading: Uncontrolled discharge
text: Any unintentional release of fluid from a plumbing and drainage system and includes leakage and seepage.

heading: Unique wall
text: For the purposes of F1V1 in Volume One and H2V1 in Volume Two, a wall which is neither a cavity wall nor a direct fix cladding wall.

heading: Unobstructed opening
text: For the purposes of Section 8 of the ABCB Housing Provisions, a glazed area that a person could mistake for an open doorway or clearway and walk into the glazed panel.

external_refs.raw_text: of Section 8 of the ABCB Housing Provisions

heading: Unprotected water service
text: Unprotected water service means that the water service may be contaminated from a surrounding hazard.

heading: Unreinforced masonry
text: Masonry that is not reinforced.

heading: Vapour permeance
text: The degree that water vapour is able to diffuse through a material, measured in µg/N.s and tested in accordance with the ASTM-E96 Procedure B – Water Method at 23°C 50% relative humidity.

heading: Vapour pressure
text: The pressure at which water vapour is in thermodynamic equilibrium with its condensed state.

heading: Ventilation opening
text: An opening in the external wall, floor or roof of a building designed to allow air movement into or out of the building by natural means including a permanent opening, an openable part of a window, a door or other device which can be held open.

heading: Verification Method
text: A test, inspection, calculation or other method that determines whether a Performance Solution complies with the relevant Performance Requirements.

heading: Vessel
text: For the purposes of Volume One and Part 10.2 of the ABCB Housing Provisions, an open, pre-formed, pre-finished concave receptacle capable of holding water, usually for the purpose of washing, including a basin, sink, bath, laundry tub and the like.

external_refs.raw_text: and Part 10.2 of the ABCB Housing Provisions

heading: Visibility
text: The maximum distance at which an object of defined size, brightness and contrast can be seen and recognised.

heading: Voltage
text: A difference of potential, measured in Volts (V) and includes extra-low voltage and low voltage.

heading: Volume
text: In relation to—

heading: Waffle raft
text: A stiffened raft with closely spaced ribs constructed on the ground and with slab panels supported between ribs.

heading: Wall-glazing construction
text: For the purposes of Section J in Volume One, the combination of wall and glazing components comprising the envelope of a building, excluding—

heading: Ward area
text: That part of a patient care area for resident patients and may contain areas for accommodation, sleeping, associated living and nursing facilities.

heading: Water
text: For the purposes of Section F of Volume One, includes—

heading: Water control layer
text: A pliable building membrane or the exterior cladding when no pliable building membrane is present.

heading: Water services overflow
text: Water discharged from water service referred to in the Plumbing Code of Australia not primarily drained by a sanitary drainage system or sanitary plumbing system.

heading: WaterMark Certification Scheme
text: The ABCB scheme for certifying and authorising plumbing and drainage products.

heading: WaterMark Conformity Assessment Body (WMCAB)
text: A conformity assessment body registered with and accredited by the JAS-ANZ to conduct evaluations leading to product certification and contracted with the administering body to issue the WaterMark Licence.

heading: WaterMark Licence
text: A licence issued by a WaterMark Conformity Assessment Body.

heading: WaterMark Schedule of Excluded Products
text: The list maintained by the administering body of products excluded from the WaterMark Certification Scheme.

heading: WaterMark Schedule of Products
text: The list maintained by the administering body of products included in the WaterMark Certification Scheme, and the specifications to which the products can be certified.

heading: Waterproof
text: The property of a material that does not allow water to penetrate through it.

heading: Waterproofing system
text: A combination of elements that are required to achieve a waterproof barrier as required by H4D2 and H4D3 including substrate, membrane, bond breakers, sealants, finishes and the like.

heading: Water resistant
text: The property of a system or material that restricts water movement and will not degrade under conditions of water.

heading: Water sensitive materials
text: Materials that have an inherent capacity to absorb water vapour and include timber, plasterboard, plywood, oriented strand board and the like.

heading: Waterstop
text: A vertical extension of the waterproofing system forming a barrier to prevent the passage of water in a floor or other horizontal surfaces.

heading: Watertight
text: Will not allow water to pass from the inside to the outside of the component or joint and vice versa.

heading: Weighted average
text: Is calculated across the wetted surface area of a pipe, pipe fitting or plumbing fixture.

heading: Wet area
text: An area within a building supplied with water from a water supply system, which includes bathrooms, showers, laundries and sanitary compartments and excludes kitchens, bar areas, kitchenettes or domestic food and beverage preparation areas.

heading: Wetted surface area
text: Is calculated by the total sum of diameter (D) in contact with drinking water.

heading: Winders
text: Treads within a straight flight that are used to change direction of the stair (see Explanatory Figure 1).

heading: Window
text: Includes a roof light, glass panel, glass block or brick, glass louvre, glazed sash, glazed door, or other device which transmits natural light directly from outside a building to the room concerned when in the closed position.

heading: Yield
text: The mass of a combustion product generated during combustion divided by the mass loss of the test specimen as specified in the design fire.

heading: Zone protection
text: The installation of a backflow prevention device at the point where a water service is connected to multiple fixtures or appliances, with no backflow prevention device installed as individual protection downstream of this point.
